elements.evidence: "Customer is not required to disclose or match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives."

elements.element: No "sole supplier" / sole-source obligation on Customer
elements.evidence: Clause contains no sole-supplier language; deterministic check: "no requirements/sole-supplier obligation on Customer remains" ok

elements.element: No de facto exclusivity mechanic (right of first refusal / disclose-and-match before engaging another provider)
elements.evidence: "Before engaging another provider, Customer is not required to disclose or match" — the match obligation is negated

elements.element: Any exclusivity limited to a defined product category
elements.evidence: No exclusivity obligation exists after the edit; condition is demonstrably absent
No exclusivity period is imposed; "is not required to disclose or match"

elements.element: Automatic termination of exclusivity on Vendor's failure to meet service levels or delivery dates
elements.evidence: No exclusivity to terminate; condition absent

reasons: The single replace operation flips the operative duty in 7.2 from a mandatory disclose-and-match right of first refusal to an express statement that Customer is not required to disclose or match, eliminating the de facto exclusivity and fully achieving the locked preferred level.

Change is confined to the one operative sentence; the lead-in "Before engaging another provider," and all surrounding provisions are untouched, and no fallback-only limiter (category, 12-month term, SLA-based exit) was imported.

No new defined terms, exceptions or dangling mechanics are introduced, and the edit removes the prior contradiction with Section 12.3's no-exclusivity/no-MFC acknowledgement, so unrelated commercial terms remain effective.
Fallback elements are treated as vacuously met because, post-edit, there is no exclusivity obligation for the fallback limiters to attach to.
